messages.author: 065110cca96a6373
messages.subject: using manual scale
parts:
Dear R users,

I am trying to plot multiple variables on a single plot, similar to
page 109 in the ggplot2 book. In my data there would be four lines,
and I would like to distinguish them using two linetypes and two
colours. I am using manual scales to do this, but it seems like there
are problems when I have both scale_colour_manual() and
scale_linetype_manual(). They work separately, but not together.
Sample code shows them working apart and how I imagine they would work
together.

Thanks in advance.

library(ggplot2)
##Sample Data##
schedule <- data.frame(
times = (0:59) + as.Date("2010-07-03"),
SMP.pages = vector(mode="integer", length=60),
PO.pages = vector(mode="integer", length=60)
)


##Works##
base <- ggplot(data = schedule, aes(x = times))
SMP.ave <- geom_hline( aes(yintercept = (689/nrow(schedule)),
colour="SMP", linetype=5) )
PO.ave <- geom_hline( aes(yintercept = (673/nrow(schedule)),
colour="PO", linetype=5) )
SMP.pages <- geom_line( aes(y = c(schedule[1, "SMP.pages"],
diff(schedule[ , "SMP.pages"], lag=1)), colour="SMP", linetype=1) )
PO.pages <- geom_line( aes(y = c(schedule[1, "PO.pages"],
diff(schedule[ , "PO.pages"], lag=1)), colour="PO", linetype=1) )

base + SMP.ave + PO.ave + SMP.pages + PO.pages +
scale_colour_manual(name = "Book", value = c("SMP" = "red", "PO" = "blue")) +
scale_y_continuous("Number of Pages") +
scale_x_date(name="Date", major="1 week", format="%d-%b")
####

##Works##
base <- ggplot(data = schedule, aes(x = times))
SMP.ave <- geom_hline( aes(yintercept = (689/nrow(schedule)),
colour="red", linetype="planned") )
PO.ave <- geom_hline( aes(yintercept = (673/nrow(schedule)),
colour="blue", linetype="planned") )
SMP.pages <- geom_line( aes(y = c(schedule[1, "SMP.pages"],
diff(schedule[ , "SMP.pages"], lag=1)), colour="red",
linetype="actual") )
PO.pages <- geom_line( aes(y = c(schedule[1, "PO.pages"],
diff(schedule[ , "PO.pages"], lag=1)), colour="blue",
linetype="actual") )

base + SMP.ave + PO.ave + SMP.pages + PO.pages +
scale_linetype_manual(name = "Class", value = c("planned" = 5,
"actual" = 1)) +
scale_y_continuous("Number of Pages") +
scale_x_date(name="Date", major="1 week", format="%d-%b")
####

##Does not work##
base <- ggplot(data = schedule, aes(x = times))
SMP.ave <- geom_hline( aes(yintercept = (689/nrow(schedule)),
colour="SMP", linetype="planned") )
PO.ave <- geom_hline( aes(yintercept = (673/nrow(schedule)),
colour="PO", linetype="planned") )
SMP.pages <- geom_line( aes(y = c(schedule[1, "SMP.pages"],
diff(schedule[ , "SMP.pages"], lag=1)), colour="SMP",
linetype="actual") )
PO.pages <- geom_line( aes(y = c(schedule[1, "PO.pages"],
diff(schedule[ , "PO.pages"], lag=1)), colour="PO", linetype="actual")
)

base + SMP.ave + PO.ave + SMP.pages + PO.pages +
scale_colour_manual(name = "Book", value = c("SMP" = "red", "PO" = "blue")) +
scale_linetype_manual(name = "Class", value = c("planned" = 5,
"actual" = 1)) +
scale_y_continuous("Number of Pages") +
scale_x_date(name="Date", major="1 week", format="%d-%b")
####

#rm(base,PO.ave,PO.pages,schedule,SMP.ave,SMP.pages)

--
Joshua Wiley
Ph.D. Student, Health Psychology
University of California, Los Angeles
http://www.joshuawiley.com/

messages.subject: Re: using manual scale
parts:
Hi Hadley,

Here is a minimal version. From what I can tell, sometime
after/during the call to ScaleManual$new(..., variable = "colour"),
three character strings are passed to col2rgb(), "blue", "blue", and
"colour1". The first two make sense, since there are two data points,
the last one causes col2rgb() to return an error message.

http://gist.github.com/463764

library(ggplot2)

sample.dat <- data.frame(x=1:2, y=1:2)

ggplot(data = sample.dat, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
geom_line( aes(colour="colour1", linetype = "line1") ) +
scale_colour_manual(name = "Colour", values = c("colour1" = "blue")) +
scale_linetype_manual(name = "Linetype", value = c("line1" = 2))


Thanks for your help,

Josh

Hi Josh,

I've made some progress on this bug, in terms of coming up with a test
case that actually shows what's going wrong:

df <- data.frame(x=1:2, y=1:2)

# Doesn't work
ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) + geom_point(aes(colour = "a", shape = "b"))
# Works
ggplot(df, aes(x, y, colour = "a", shape = "b")) + geom_point()

Hadley
